db_metadata.description: Mature miRNA family sequences (human (hsa)) built from miRBase CURRENT. Family grouping by seed sequence (positions 2-8, canonical functional definition).
db_metadata.warning: Generated by scripts/build_mirbase_data.py from miRBase CURRENT. Re-run after each miRBase release update.
db_metadata.family_grouping: Seed sequence positions 2-8 (canonical miRNA family definition). Members sharing the same seed are cross-reactivity candidates for the stemloop RT primer overhang region.

test_results.description: Core let-7 5p members share same family (Chen 2005 Fig.7)
hsa-miR-98-5p shares let-7 seed — should be in let-7 family (miRBase v22.1)
let-7 3p strands must NOT share family with 5p strands (opposite strand, different seed)
test_results.reason: Groups correctly assigned to distinct families.
test_results.notes: 5p and 3p strands have different seeds — seed-based grouping correctly separates them.

test_results.description: miR-17, miR-20a, miR-106a, miR-93 share AAAGUGC seed — expected same group
test_results.notes: Seed-based grouping uses the 7-nt seed (pos 2-8) so the family label will be 'miR-1_AAAGUGC' not 'mir-17' as in canonical miFam.dat. Membership is correct; label divergence is an EXPECTED limitation of seed-based classification.

test_results.description: miR-200b/200c/429 share AAUACUG seed; miR-200a/141 share AACACUG seed. Seed-based grouping CORRECTLY splits them into two groups.
test_results.notes: Canonical miRBase miFam.dat groups all five (miR-200a/b/c + miR-141 + miR-429) into one family. Seed-based classification correctly reflects the two distinct seeds (AAUACUG vs AACACUG), which matters for RT primer cross-reactivity analysis: miR-200a will NOT react with miR-200b primers at the overhang level.

test_results.description: miR-200a and miR-141 share AACACUG seed — expected same seed group

test_results.notes: miR-21-5p may be a small cluster or paired with miR-590-5p (same seed). No major cross-reactivity family concern for stem-loop RT primer design.
